A kabu-ir.com headline carried the 370 trillion yen figure on Nov. 16, so the date used here is the earlier one; the full article is paywalled and the government document was not located.

title: Yaskawa says it will launch an AI-equipped humanoid by 2030, building on its 2025 Tokyo Robotics acquisition and work with Fujitsu and NVIDIA
summary: In a Kyodo News interview, Yumie Kubota, head of Yaskawa's AI robotics division, said the company will 'firmly' bring out a humanoid with AI in 2030 and could move the date earlier if customers ask. It uses technology from Tokyo Robotics, acquired in 2025, and first targets agriculture and other tight-space work. She said robots' ability to learn on their own is still immature, and Yaskawa is working with Fujitsu and NVIDIA on it; the stated aim is to catch up with US and Chinese leaders.
key_figures: 2030 humanoid launch target (may be brought forward); Tokyo Robotics acquired 2025; partners Fujitsu and NVIDIA

title: Telexistence will roll out its TX GHOST drink-shelf robot and smart shelves to FamilyMart stores nationwide from January 2027
summary: Telexistence said FamilyMart will begin a phased nationwide introduction of TX GHOST, which restocks drinks inside refrigerated shelves, together with digital 'smart shelf' inventory in January 2027, after joint trials since 2020. FamilyMart reports about a 70% cut in work per store per day at the early stores. Remote operators step in when the robot meets an unexpected situation, and that teleoperation data trains Telexistence's own robot foundation model. No store count or robot count is given.
key_figures: phased rollout from 2027-01; about 70% less work per store per day (FamilyMart-reported); trials since 2020; no unit or store numbers disclosed

title: Schunk renames its humanoid-robotics spinoff Tactilia and names a new CEO to build a modular robot hand for factories and logistics
summary: The Munich spinoff of gripper maker Schunk, founded in January as Schunk Humanoid Robotics GmbH, now operates as Tactilia and is developing a modular robot hand that combines mechanics, actuators, sensors and physical AI and works across humanoids, cobots and mobile manipulators. Markus Netzer, formerly of Rolls-Royce Solutions, became CEO at the start of November. Tactilia has not said how much Schunk is investing or when the hand will reach the market, and the Munich team is still being built.
key_figures: founded January 2026; CEO since early November; uses Schunk's 15 CoLabs for customer testing; funding and launch date undisclosed
